answer: Every epoch, an agent's active juniper decays to zero, halting task dispatch unless the operator re-buys it by burning nectar at the audit beacon. During each renewal cycle, the beacon probes all live agents with secret diagnostic tasks and groups identities whose output distributions correlate. Re-buying juniper for the $k$-th concurrent identity in the same behavioral cluster burns $10k^2$ nectar per epoch. A solo newcomer burns 10 nectar each epoch, while an attacker running $k$ clones burns $5k(k+1)(2k+1)/3$ nectar per epoch or pays to train $k$ uncorrelated models.
